title: Human Rights Watch: Kast's Security Reform Doesn't Meet Chile's International Obligations
detail: Human Rights Watch's Americas director, Juanita Goebertus, said September 1 that President Kast's ACOT constitutional security reform 'no se ajusta a las obligaciones internacionales de Chile' (does not align with Chile's international obligations), warning that its proposed fifth type of constitutional state of exception — an eight-month presidential emergency power renewable without prior congressional authorization — would grant the president 'una autoridad prácticamente ilimitada' (virtually unlimited authority) and endanger rights to freedom of assembly and association. HRW also flagged the reform's vague criteria for designating groups as terrorist or criminal organizations without specifying legal consequences, its warrantless communications-interception powers, and proposed differentiated prison regimes restricting visits and benefits. The organization urged Congress to reject the reform, calling it 'una peligrosa usurpación de poder' (a dangerous usurpation of power). Kast rejected withdrawing the bill the same day, telling reporters 'el debate recién está comenzando' (the debate is just beginning) even as the government had already downgraded the measure from 'suma urgencia' to 'urgencia simple' in Congress.

media.caption: Human Rights Watch warns Kast's security reform threatens fundamental rights — September 1, 2026

title: Kast Supervises 'Jaukén 2026' Military Deployment in Magallanes, Skips Official September 11 Ceremony at La Moneda
detail: President Kast traveled to Punta Arenas September 1 to oversee joint Armed Forces operations in Magallanes — an Amphibious Task Force with naval squadron units, submarines, Marine Infantry, Naval Aviation and Special Forces conducting the winter exercise 'Jaukén 2026' — days after Chile's protest note over Argentine Air Force comments on the Strait of Magellan. Kast said the deployment reaffirmed that 'the Strait of Magallanes, beyond any debate, is under Chilean sovereignty,' with the visit acquiring extra weight ahead of Argentine President Javier Milei's planned trip to Santiago. Separately, Kast confirmed he will not hold an official La Moneda ceremony for the September 11 anniversary of the 1973 coup, saying he will instead be 'deployed, as always, in regions' and treating the date like any other working day; he also ruled out announcing pardons for security-force personnel convicted over the 2019 estallido social on the anniversary, while defending his authority to grant individual humanitarian pardons case by case.

media.caption: Kast supervises the Jaukén 2026 military exercise in Magallanes — September 1, 2026

title: IMACEC Falls 1.5% in July — Worst Reading in Three Years as Mining Output Plunges 9.3%
detail: Chile's Central Bank reported July 2026 IMACEC contracted 1.5% year-on-year — reversing June's +2.4% expansion and marking the index's worst performance in more than three years — with the seasonally adjusted series down 1.7% month-on-month and 2.1% annualized. Mining output plunged 9.3% YoY on lower ore grades, scheduled maintenance and adverse weather that disrupted operations; the non-mining IMACEC fell a milder 0.3% YoY. Goods production contracted 3.2% annually and services fell 0.7% (education hit hardest by weather-related school closures), while commerce grew a modest 0.7%, partially offsetting the broader weakness. The Central Bank attributed part of the decline to 'condiciones climáticas' affecting productive establishments but offered no forward guidance on recession risk; the reading complicates the government's economic-emergency narrative after June's data had narrowly averted a technical recession.

sources.name: Diario y Radio Universidad de Chile

media.caption: IMACEC contracts 1.5% in July 2026, the worst reading in three years — September 1, 2026
